nodes.name: agnosticism_lint.py
nodes.summary: Static "no project nouns" lint that proves the generic graph layer stays project-agnostic: it scans the enumerated generic-layer sources (runner/graph_*.py, runner/vault_*.py, runner/dev_graph/**, the vault template, the obsidian-graph skill) for a denylist of reference-instance proper nouns and domain terms and reports every file:line:noun hit. Pure, deterministic and Claude-free — it reads and reports, writes nothing and evaluates no gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses as the result contract, a single compiled word-boundary case-insensitive regex alternation built from a frozenset denylist, and a `python -m` CLI entry point with distinct exit codes (0 clean / 1 violations / 3 error).

nodes.name: LintViolation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass recording one denylisted project noun found in a generic-layer source: the repo-relative path, 1-based line, the verbatim matched noun, and the stripped offending line for an actionable report.

nodes.name: LintReport
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the outcome of a generic-layer scan — every scanned file plus every violation in (path, line) order — with an `ok` property that is true only when no project noun was found.

nodes.name: scan_text
nodes.summary: Pure matcher that finds every denylisted noun in a text, returning (line_number, matched_noun, stripped_line) tuples in document order. Word-boundary and case-insensitive matching keeps whole-word nouns from hitting substrings of unrelated words.

nodes.name: iter_generic_layer_files
nodes.summary: Resolves the GENERIC_LAYER_GLOBS to the authored text files worth scanning: de-duplicated, sorted by repo-relative POSIX path for determinism, restricted to the allowed text suffixes, and excluding vendored segments such as the Obsidian app directory.

nodes.name: lint_generic_layer
nodes.summary: Top-level scan entry point: reads every enumerated generic-layer source as BOM-tolerant UTF-8 and collects a LintViolation per denylisted-noun hit into a LintReport. Never raises on a leak — it reports one, leaving the non-zero exit to the CLI.

nodes.name: format_report
nodes.summary: Renders a LintReport as human-readable text: a one-line OK summary when clean, or a FAIL block listing every path:line:noun with the offending line plus remediation guidance pointing the project-specific fact back to the per-project config or vault.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python -m runner.agnosticism_lint`: parses an optional --repo-root (otherwise auto-discovering it), runs the lint, and returns exit code 0 when clean, 1 when project nouns leaked, or 3 on an unexpected error.

nodes.name: consortium_composition.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic evaluator for the Horizon Europe consortium-composition condition: it reads the four thresholds and their verbatim citations out of the Tier 1 participation rules and the partner records out of the Tier 3 registry, then reports whether the consortium is met and which of the four limbs fails. No threshold is supplied from programme knowledge and no partner fact is inferred — it reads, evaluates and reports, writing nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Country is modelled as a pseudonymous slot (C1, C2, …) carrying only a Member State / Associated Country class, so the evaluator can never see or leak a real country name. Evaluation is order-independent by construction: every grouping sorts by partner id before a setdefault, so a last-wins dict cannot silently break reproducibility.

nodes.name: CompositionError
nodes.summary: Fail-closed exception raised when Tier 1 or Tier 3 cannot be read as the evaluator needs it. A missing threshold or an unreadable partner record is never defaulted, because guessing either would decide eligibility on an invention.

nodes.name: Citation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding one verbatim span of a Tier 1 source — quote, source document, page and section — tagged with the limb of the condition it evidences so a result carries the text it was decided on.

nodes.name: CompositionRule
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying the composition condition exactly as Tier 1 states it: the four minimum thresholds, whether affiliated entities count, the verbatim rule text, the supporting citations, and the source artifact path.

nodes.name: Beneficiary
nodes.summary: One partner record reduced to what the condition asks about: partner id, pseudonymous country slot, slot class, and the independent / is_beneficiary flags, with a `counts` property that is true only when both hold.

nodes.name: CompositionResult
nodes.summary: The verdict of evaluating one consortium: whether the condition is met, which partners counted or were excluded, the distinct and class-partitioned country slots, the failed limbs, a satisfying selection, and the thresholds and citations it was judged against. Its `status` and `reason` properties are derived from those fields, so the printed sentence cannot drift from the verdict.

nodes.name: Scenario
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass pairing one consortium variant — its name, the question it answers, and the partner ids it includes — with the CompositionResult that variant produced.

nodes.name: _load_json
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON object from disk, failing closed with a CompositionError naming the path when the file is absent, not parseable, or does not hold an object at the top level.

nodes.name: _citation
nodes.summary: Builds a Citation from a verbatim-span block of the Tier 1 rule artifact, type-checking quote, source document, page and section and tagging the span with the limb it evidences; returns None when the span is absent or malformed.

nodes.name: load_composition_rule
nodes.summary: Reads the composition condition out of the Tier 1 extracted participation rules: the four integer thresholds, the affiliated-entities flag, the verbatim rule text and its citations, raising CompositionError rather than defaulting anything so no threshold ever comes from programme knowledge.

nodes.name: load_partners
nodes.summary: Reads the Tier 3 partner registry into a tuple of Beneficiary records, requiring a partner id, a country slot and a slot class on every entry and raising CompositionError on any missing or mistyped field rather than guessing a value that would decide eligibility.

nodes.name: partners_by_capability_basis
nodes.summary: Groups partner ids by their recorded `capability_basis`, reading the fact from the Tier 3 registry so a CLI default or a report can never disagree with it; always exposes the 'derived' and 'fictional' groups, sorted.

nodes.name: evaluate_composition
nodes.summary: The core pure evaluation: filters partners down to independent beneficiaries, collapses them onto distinct country slots, classifies each slot as Member State, Associated Country or neither, tests the four limbs (counting only the further eligible slots for the 'other countries' limb so one slot is never spent twice), and returns a CompositionResult with a satisfying selection when all limbs pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Order-independence is explicit: counted partners are sorted by id before every setdefault, so two partners disagreeing about a shared slot's class resolve identically on every run.

nodes.name: evaluate_scenarios
nodes.summary: Evaluates the three readings the consortium analysis asks for: all partners, the derived partners alone without the fictional gap partners, and each gap partner removed in turn — the redundancy question of whether the condition still holds if any single unconfirmed partner withdraws.

nodes.name: format_scenarios
nodes.summary: Renders the scenario table a human reads: one line per scenario with its met/not-met status, partner count and derived reason sentence, followed by the Tier 1 citations the verdict rests on.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python -m runner.consortium_composition`: resolves the repo root, loads the Tier 1 rule and Tier 3 partners, derives the derived/gap partner sets from the registry unless overridden by --derived/--gap, prints the scenario table, and exits 0 when the condition is met, 1 when it is not, or 3 when a tier could not be read.

nodes.name: leakage_scan.py
nodes.summary: The anonymity scan guarding the blind-assessment lane: it checks that no reference-instance organisation name, person, place, web address or project identifier appears in Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5 or the vault. Two mechanisms do the work — a word scan over a denylist derived from the agnosticism lint's PROJECT_NOUNS (partitioned into identity, re-identifying and deliberately scoped-out nouns), and a structural pseudonymity check that reads the real country lists out of Tier 1 and fails on any country name, URL or email in a Tier 3 self-description.
nodes.languageNotes: The report deliberately separates `ok` (no new leak — the regression guard) from `clean` (no leak at all — the constraint itself), with KNOWN_PRE_EXISTING_LEAKS pinning each recorded leak to its path and reason so a known leak can never be reported as clean. The denylist is derived from PROJECT_NOUNS rather than re-typed, so a noun added there is scanned at once. Known scope gap: SCAN_GLOBS cover Tier 3/4/5 and the vault but do not reach docs/integrations/.

nodes.name: LeakageError
nodes.summary: Fail-closed exception raised when the scan cannot read a source it needs — notably the Tier 1 country list — on the principle that a check which cannot run must not report clean.

nodes.name: LeakageViolation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass recording one leak: its path (a file path, or a file plus JSON field path for a record-level hit), line number (0 when located structurally), the verbatim matched text, a snippet, the kind of leak (identity noun, country name, web address or email), and whether the path is a recorded pre-existing leak.

nodes.name: LeakageReport
nodes.summary: The outcome of a scan, with three outcomes rather than two: `ok` (no new leak, what a regression guard answers), `clean` (no leak at all, what the anonymity constraint asks), and a `format` method that renders OK, 'OK, NOT CLEAN' with the recorded pre-existing leaks, or FAIL with remediation guidance.

nodes.name: leakage_denylist
nodes.summary: Compiles the scan's matcher: a single word-boundary, case-insensitive alternation over LEAKAGE_NOUNS plus any operator-supplied extra nouns, sorted longest-first so an overlapping longer noun wins the report.

nodes.name: scan_text
nodes.summary: Pure matcher applying a compiled pattern line by line to a text, returning (line_number, matched_text, stripped_line) tuples in document order. Reused by both the word scan and the prose leg of the pseudonymity check.

nodes.name: iter_vault_roots
nodes.summary: Discovers every project vault by reading the `vault_path` out of each graph.config.yaml, skipping the generic template and test fixtures, so a vault is scanned wherever it actually lives. Conservative on failure: an unreadable config or a missing PyYAML widens the scan to the config's own directory rather than narrowing it.

nodes.name: iter_scanned_files
nodes.summary: Resolves the scan scope — the Tier 3/4/5 globs plus every discovered vault root — into a deterministic, de-duplicated, sorted list of text files, dropping non-text suffixes and vendored path segments.

nodes.name: scan_tree
nodes.summary: The word-scan entry point: reads every in-scope file in Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5 and the vault and collects a LeakageViolation per denylist hit, flagging hits at recorded paths as pre_existing so they do not fail the scan.

nodes.name: real_country_names
nodes.summary: Reads the real country names — Member States, Associated Countries and Overseas Countries and Territories — out of the Tier 1 participation rules rather than listing them, so the pseudonymity check cannot drift from the General Annexes. Fails closed with LeakageError when Tier 1 is unreadable.

nodes.name: _iter_strings
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a parsed JSON tree yielding (json_path, string) for every string value, so a record-level hit can be located by field path rather than by line number.

nodes.name: _iter_globbed
nodes.summary: Shared resolver for both pseudonymity legs: expands a glob set to existing files, deterministically sorted and de-duplicated, minus the declared exemptions — one resolver so an exemption can never apply to the JSON leg and not the prose leg.

nodes.name: scan_partner_records
nodes.summary: The structural pseudonymity check and the only mechanism that catches a country name: it builds a pattern from the Tier 1 country lists and matches it, along with URL and email patterns, against every string in the in-scope Tier 3 JSON self-descriptions (located by field path) and every line of the in-scope Tier 3 prose. An absent artifact yields no violation; an unreadable Tier 1 raises LeakageError.

nodes.name: _read_extra_nouns
nodes.summary: Reads the operator's noun extension file — one noun per line, comments skipped — which is deliberately kept outside the repository so that writing those names into the branch does not itself become the leak the scan exists to prevent.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python -m runner.leakage_scan`: resolves the repo root, runs the word scan with any --extra-nouns extension and the pseudonymity record check, merges both into one report, and exits 0 when no new leak was found (still printing 'NOT CLEAN' for recorded leaks), 1 on a new leak, or 3 when a needed source could not be read.
